conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s just 10 questions about the past seven days, and it helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can show up after childbirth. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell us someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers, and we’ll go at your pace.

To start, could you tell me: in the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi, Sarah… I guess I’ve laughed a little—mostly when my husband makes silly faces at the baby—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Things that used to crack me up now feel kind of “meh.” So I’d say it’s been harder overall.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes I can, but it doesn’t feel as natural—like I have to remind myself to laugh, and even then it’s kind of muted.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to some things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes to help—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. A lot of the time I’m just tired and hoping I can get through the day without feeling overwhelmed.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby was extra fussy and I caught myself thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right—like maybe my milk isn’t good enough or I missed some cue. Deep down I know it’s probably not my fault, but those thoughts still pop in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most days, at least once, I’ll suddenly feel my heart racing even though nothing’s happening—like when the baby’s napping and the house is quiet. I’ll start imagining weird scenarios: what if he stops breathing, or what if I drop him, even though he’s right there in the crib and I’m just folding laundry. So, yeah, it feels like there’s this constant low-level worry running in the background.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panic, but a couple of times—especially at night when I’m trying to fall back asleep after feeding—I’ll get this sudden “what-if” rush, like something bad is about to happen. My chest feels tight, and I have to sit up and take slow breaths. It passes after a few minutes, but it leaves me wired and makes getting back to sleep even harder.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… some days it feels like the minute I finish one thing, two more pop up. I’ll finally get the baby settled and realize I haven’t eaten or the laundry’s overflowing, and I just want to sit down but I can’t. I’m not falling apart, but I do end most days feeling like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s not so much that I’m feeling desperately unhappy—it’s more that my mind keeps spinning with baby stuff and “what-ifs.” I lie down and suddenly remember I didn’t order diapers or I start worrying about his breathing, and then I’m wide awake. Most nights it takes me at least an hour to drift off, and if he wakes up right after I finally doze off, it’s hard to settle again.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time, but it comes and goes. Like yesterday evening, I was rocking the baby and suddenly felt this wave of “I miss myself” or “I miss the old normal,” and my eyes got watery. It’s not every day, and it’s not all day, but yeah—those moments hit.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really. I’ve felt teary a couple of times, but the tears don’t actually fall—more like a lump in my throat than a full-on cry. The last time I really sobbed was over a week ago, and even that was short.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’m tired and overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel more like “me” again and be able to enjoy my baby without all this worry.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item self-report (EPDS-style questions)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Diminished enjoyment/pleasure (laughing, looking forward to events)  
- Frequent, unprovoked anxiety and nocturnal “what-if” ruminations with mild autonomic arousal (tight chest, racing heart)  
- Intermittent tearfulness and subjective sadness (“I miss myself”)  
- Sleep-onset and return-to-sleep problems driven by intrusive worries rather than infant demands alone  
- Self-criticism / inappropriate guilt regarding infant care (“my milk isn’t good enough”)  
- Sense of being overwhelmed / “treading water” most days

Pattern  
Mood and anxiety symptoms present >2 weeks, variable intensity, no anhedonia or hopelessness all day every day; no suicidal or self-harm ideation reported.

Risk indicators  
- Sub-threshold depressive mood with preserved attachment to infant  
- Mild–moderate generalized and nocturnal anxiety  
- No current suicidal ideation → safety risk absent at time of screening

Screening summary  
Findings suggest clinically significant postpartum anxiety with mild depressive features; does not meet full criteria ascertainable in this brief screen. Recommend routine follow-up, psychoeducation, and consideration of structured assessment (EPDS, GAD-7) for level-of-care determination.
